context:
Provenance manifest, not a bigger COUNT check. setup() writes a single-row
`benchbox_staging_manifest` table (benchmark, scale, spec_version,
source_digest, created_at). is_setup() reads it and returns True only when every
field matches the current run. A missing manifest returns False, so every
pre-existing database self-heals on first use -- safe by construction.
Implement the manifest read/write ONCE in transactional/benchmark_base.py so
transaction_primitives and write_primitives cannot drift.
description:
Supersedes transactional-staging-reuse-ignores-provenance, dropped the same day: verification ladders are
create-time-only in this tracker, so a lint finding on a rung can only be
fixed by recreating the item.

benchbox/core/transaction_primitives/benchmark.py::is_setup and
benchbox/core/write_primitives/benchmark.py::is_setup decide whether staging
tables are ready using only `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM <table>` and returning True on
any non-zero count. There is no scale, seed, spec-version or source-data check.

benchbox/core/transactional/benchmark_base.py::_prepare_operation then does
`if operation.requires_setup and not self.is_setup(connection): setup(...)`.

CONSEQUENCE: a staging set left over from a scale-0.01 run satisfies is_setup for
a scale-1.0 run. setup() is skipped, the benchmark executes against the wrong
data volume, and the run is reported as a PASS. This is a silent wrong-results
bug, not a hygiene issue -- the timings are meaningless but indistinguishable
from valid ones in the result bundle.

OBSERVED 2026-07-29 during release-gate stage 1; a draft exists at
~/.todo-db/finding-drafts/benchbox/duckdb-reuse-staleness-2026-07-29.md.

anti_patterns.dont: fix this by widening the COUNT check to compare row counts against expected scale
anti_patterns.instead: record explicit provenance at setup time and compare it
anti_patterns.why: row counts collide across seeds and across partially-loaded databases, so it trades a silent wrong answer for a subtler one

anti_patterns.dont: implement the manifest separately in transaction_primitives and write_primitives
anti_patterns.instead: one implementation in benchmark_base.py, both overrides delegate
anti_patterns.why: these two is_setup overrides already drifted (different table lists, different quoting) which is how the bug survived review

anti_patterns.dont: silence the extra rebuild by shipping a migration that back-fills manifests for existing databases
anti_patterns.instead: accept one rebuild and note it in the changelog
anti_patterns.why: back-filling asserts a provenance nobody actually verified -- it manufactures the false confidence this item exists to remove

anti_patterns.dont: treat a missing manifest as 'probably fine, reuse it'
anti_patterns.instead: missing manifest returns False and forces one rebuild
anti_patterns.why: every pre-existing database on every developer machine lacks the manifest; defaulting to reuse preserves the exact bug being fixed

preserves.behavior: Intentional cross-benchmark reuse of TPC-H loaded databases (read_primitives etc.) still works when the manifest matches; this narrows reuse, it does not disable it.
No change to result bundle schema or to any published field.
The manifest table is created inside the same connection/transaction discipline as the staging tables; a failed setup still rolls back via _rollback_connection_after_error.

prior_art.concept: shared base already owns _prepare_operation and the abstract is_setup/setup contract; the manifest helpers belong here, not duplicated per spec
existing in-database ledger table pattern (NOT_VALIDATED marker) for recording provenance alongside the data it describes
reuse-aware pruning keyed databases_root/platform/benchmark/scale -- documents the intended reuse boundary the manifest must enforce in-database

verifications.command: uv run python -c "import inspect;from benchbox.core.transaction_primitives.benchmark import TransactionPrimitivesBenchmark as T;from benchbox.core.write_primitives.benchmark import WritePrimitivesBenchmark as W;assert all('manifest' in inspect.getsource(c.is_setup) for c in (T,W))"
verifications.description: Both is_setup overrides consult a provenance manifest rather than COUNT alone
verifications.expected: FAILS (exit 1) on the unfixed tree: both overrides decide readiness on SELECT COUNT(*) alone. Exits 0 once each requires a matching manifest.

verifications.description: Staging provenance unit tests pass (pytest exits 5 if the file is absent, so this rung proves the tests exist)
verifications.expected: scale-mismatch forces rebuild; matching manifest skips rebuild; legacy populated-but-unmanifested database forces rebuild
